correctness.rationale: The normalized nonzero vectors and orthogonality over F₃ construct exactly the stated 13 points and 13 lines; the independently replayed pair-incidence test places each pair on one four-point line. The set version enumerates all binary assignments as subsets of those 13 points, accepts exactly the subsets meeting each line nontrivially and not fully, and inserts exactly the single-point symmetric difference edges between accepted subsets. Breadth-first search from every one of the 468 accepted states gives all shortest distances. The independent report gives 234 states of each weight 6 and 7, degree 3 and 702 edges, all searches connected, radius and diameter 13, the exact stated common sphere list and the complement as the unique antipode at each root. Counting each distinct pair once gives 109278 pairs; the entire joint histogram agrees with RESULT.md, with 83070 defect zero and 26208 defect two. Hamming is a lower bound and fixes distance parity because moves toggle one bit. The proof is a full finite exhaustion for this plane, not an extrapolation. evidence: The earlier six-set geometry has four triple secants forming a frame, so legal one-point extensions are exactly the three points outside those four lines; this explains cubicity from earlier ingredients. Two distinct six-point states have at most one common legal seven-point neighbor (their union). The resulting two-step graph has degree six, so it exhausts the six-regular exchange graph. Thus even flip distances are twice the exchange distances; the earlier radius, diameter and even shells give genuine partial coverage. The diameter 13 also follows from the exchange bound plus one cross-edge and the Hamming-13 complement.

For an opposite-side target, the flip distance is one plus twice the minimum exchange distance to any six-set contained in the target. The prior shell counts do not give the distribution of these minima jointly with Hamming distance. Even-shell marginals also do not give the same-side Hamming pairing.
The earlier oval result makes the extra move depend on a blocking union for a pair of four-point ovals, not on these named coloring endpoints.

value.rationale: The named-coloring graph of the classical ternary plane is a natural legal-move space, and Hamming comparison separates always-achievable direct flips from genuine detours. The sharp additive two and roughly one-quarter obstruction census give a reusable finite benchmark: they answer a question that neither knowing the solution count, the cubic graph's diameter, nor knowing exchange-graph distance marginals answers. No larger-plane law or general algorithm is asserted.
